drivingQuestion: In what case do R' Eliezer and R' Yosei disagree?
outcomeNote: the gemara delimits and explains the mishna's dispute

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ בְּנִיטָּל בְּאִגְדּוֹ — כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי. כִּי פְּלִיגִי
segments.en: «GEMARA:» The Gemara narrows the dispute: «If» the bolt «can be moved by the rope» with which it is attached to the door, «everyone agrees» that it is considered part of the door, and one may secure the door with it. «When» Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Eliezer «disagree,»

segments.he: בְּשֶׁאֵינוֹ נִיטָּל בְּאִיגְדּוֹ, דְּמָר סָבַר: כֵּיוָן דְּיֵשׁ בְּרֹאשׁוֹ גְּלוֹסְטְרָא — תּוֹרַת כְּלִי עָלָיו. וּמָר סָבַר: כֵּיוָן דְּאֵינוֹ נִיטָּל בְּאִיגְדּוֹ — לֹא.
segments.en: it is «in» a case «where it cannot be picked up by its rope,» as it is too thin to bear the weight of the bolt. «As» this «Sage,» Rabbi Yosei, «maintains: Since it has a knob at its end, it has the status of a vessel,» and one is therefore permitted to secure the door with it. «And» this «Sage,» Rabbi Eliezer, «maintains: Since it cannot be picked up by its rope, no,» it is not considered a proper vessel merely because of the knob, and consequently, its use is prohibited on Shabbat.
